sections.preamble: You answer questions about a single medical image. Follow the answer format requested in the user message exactly.

content.text:
This is one axial slice of a T2-weighted fat-suppressed MRI (radiological convention: patient right on image left, anterior at top). It contains a fibrous soft-tissue tumor.

The left panel is the clean image; the right panel shows numbered marks. Choose the ONE mark that lies inside the tumor, as close to its centre as possible. End your reply with a final line exactly: ANSWER: <mark number>

content.thinking:
I'm trying to pinpoint the tumor's location, noting kidneys and a large intermediate-signal mass in the middle-left abdominal region, roughly spanning x=380-600, y=250-700, with several candidate coordinate markers in that area suggesting a possible fibrous soft-tissue mass like a desmoid tumor.

But I also notice a heterogeneous bright region near the anterior abdominal wall at the top, which could instead represent the actual tumor, possibly with an infiltrative pattern typical of an abdominal wall desmoid, spanning roughly x=190-400, y=80-230, with several markers located within that upper mass.

content.text:
The most likely tumor is the heterogeneous, bright, infiltrative mass in the anterior abdominal wall at the top left of the image. It spans roughly x 190–390 and y 80–230 in the left panel. This is a judgement call: the large intermediate-signal region in the centre of the image could also be the tumor, and I could not rule it out.

Two marks fall inside the anterior mass: 1381 and 1383. Mark 1381 sits near the lower edge, close to dark strands at the margin. Mark 1383 sits in solid bright tissue closer to the middle of the mass, so I chose it. Mark 1570 is borderline at the left edge and I ruled it out.

ANSWER: 1383
